papers.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 147 loci associated with obstructive sleep apnea
papers.abstract: The genetic components underlying obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted the largest GWAS meta-analysis (OSA; Ncases= 232,292; Ncontrols= 1,259,390) using European ancestry genetic data from five countries. We identified 147 independent loci and estimated SNP-based heritability at 16%. We report six independent loci in a separate African population meta-analysis (Ncases= 46,834; Ncontrols= 149,192). Spatially resolved gene enrichment in neural circuits involved synaptic transmission, including GABAergic and glutamatergic signalling, and cytoskeletal remodelling. OSA-derived polygenic risk scores predicted clinician-ascertained OSA status, Fitbit-derived sleep features, and symptom-based OSA risk and snoring in participants of diverse ancestral backgrounds. We identified putative causal relationships with ADHD, depression, multisite chronic pain, body mass index, and schizophrenia, among others. Our findings demonstrate a substantial genetic component underlying OSA risk beyond shared genetic effects with body mass index, implicating neurobiological pathways related to synaptic function and corticothalamic feedback loops.

papers.title: Frontoparietal Hyperconnectivity as a Single-Subject Neural Signature of Chronic Tinnitus
papers.abstract: Chronic tinnitus, the persistent perception of phantom sound, affects 14 to 15\% of adults yet lacks a validated neurophysiological biomarker, in part because group-average EEG analyses obscure the individual heterogeneity that defines the condition. In a multi-site case-control study of 544 participants (268 with tinnitus, mean age 45.4 {+/-} 16.1 years, 52\% female) across seven independent international sites, we applied normative modelling to quantify how far each person's resting-state EEG deviates from age- and hearing-adjusted healthy norms. Fusing spectral-power and connectivity deviations, a classifier detected tinnitus with an area under the curve of 0.832 under site-grouped cross-validation of precomputed normative features. The single most discriminative feature, rank-stable across all seven sites, was theta-band right orbitofrontal (pars orbitalis) connectivity, which dominated attribution by roughly an order of magnitude. Theta hyperconnectivity spanned frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks while primary auditory cortex showed negligible involvement, favouring failed top-down gating over bottom-up auditory overactivity. Features identifying tinnitus presence were orthogonal to symptom severity. These findings reframe chronic tinnitus as a frontoparietal attention-network disorder and nominate right orbitofrontal theta hyperconnectivity as a site-robust diagnostic feature. Data were collected within the TIDE project (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06520865).

papers.title: Smartphone-Based Assessment of Cognitive Variability in Alzheimer Disease
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Repeated smartphone testing can measure cognitive inconsistency that a single clinic visit cannot capture. We evaluated cognitive variability and everyday phone use in biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer disease (AD). METHODS: Older adults with mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild AD dementia and cognitively unimpaired controls used Smartphone Monitoring Assessment in Real Time-Alzheimer (SMART-A) on their own phones. Response-time variability was adjusted for task demand and practice. RESULTS: Among 26 participants with cognitive data (14 controls, 12 AD), the four-marker variability composite was higher in AD (Hedges g = 1.29; 95% confidence interval, 0.53-2.06; P = .003) and correlated with baseline Montreal Cognitive Assessment score (r = -0.60; P = .001). Memory-task accuracy was lower in AD at all four trials, and 64.5% versus 98.2% of sessions reached delayed recall (P < .001). Median phone-use bouts were shorter in AD (2.4 vs 5.4 minutes; P = .031), without a detectable pickup-frequency difference. Diary-reported bedtime was earlier in AD; sensor-derived sleep, activity, and mobility showed no statistically detectable differences. None of the 19 cross-domain contrasts survived false-discovery-rate correction. DISCUSSION: SMART-A supported repeated assessment over months in biomarker-confirmed AD. Cognitive variability, memory-task progression, and phone-use duration are promising complementary measures, requiring independent validation of reliability, incremental value, and sensitivity to clinical change.

papers.title: Cycle-based neurostimulation for control of circadian brain network dynamics in human epilepsy
papers.abstract: Biological rhythms modulate symptoms of brain disorders, yet brain stimulation therapies largely overlook the temporal organization of pathological brain states. Harnessing these rhythms could improve therapeutic efficacy. Here, we show that circadian coordination of hippocampal network connectivity is a biomarker of therapeutic response to responsive neurostimulation in epilepsy. Using longitudinal electrocorticography from individuals with bitemporal epilepsy, we find that alignment of circadian connectivity rhythms between the left and right hippocampus predicts seizure reduction. The daily distribution of stimulation also predicts how these rhythms evolve over months. We capture these dynamics using a nonlinear Kuramoto oscillator model and demonstrate that optimizing stimulation timing in silico can improve predicted circadian network alignment. Our findings establish a cycle-based, control-theoretic framework for modelling and potentially reshaping brain network rhythms, offering new opportunities for personalized neurostimulation in epilepsy and other neurological and psychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Wearable-measured 24-hour heart rate variability and neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Objective To examine wearable heart rate measures in age-related macular degeneration (AMD), reporting an exploratory observation in neovascular AMD. Results This cross-sectional All of Us analysis used minute-level Fitbit heart rate from adults aged [≥]50 years with eye care records. Among the 55 participants with neovascular AMD, the mean date of complete Fitbit recording days fell a median of 1.9 years after the first neovascular AMD diagnosis code. The 7259 comparators had no AMD. The planned primary test, sleeping heart rate with any AMD, was not statistically significant (odds ratio [OR] per 10 beats/min, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.97-1.29). Higher standard deviation of 5-minute average beat intervals (SDANN), a secondary measure, was associated with higher odds of neovascular AMD versus no AMD (OR per 10 ms, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.04-1.21], uncorrected P = 0.002, Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.051 for 22 comparisons). In an exploratory comparison with non-neovascular AMD, the OR was 1.20 (95% CI, 1.08-1.32). After 24-hour heart rate adjustment, the OR versus no AMD was 1.13 (95% CI, 1.04-1.24). No associations were detected for epiretinal membrane or cataract. This exploratory observation warrants testing in recordings preceding conversion.

papers.title: Interrater agreement of seizure onset and spread in scalp EEG
papers.abstract: Objective. Faster seizure spread on intracranial EEG has been linked to worse surgical outcome. If contralateral spread on scalp EEG carried similar prognostic information, it could identify poor resection candidates before intracranial monitoring and direct them toward neuromodulation sooner. Testing this first requires that experts reliably annotate spread on scalp EEG. The interrater agreement for seizure spread detection on scalp EEG is unknown; prior scalp EEG reliability studies have focused mainly on seizure detection. We quantified expert agreement on the laterality, channels, and timing of seizure onset and contralateral spread. Methods. We retrospectively analyzed 79 seizures from 48 patients undergoing presurgical evaluation at a single center. Three board certified epileptologists independently marked the time and channels of onset and contralateral spread for each seizure. We measured agreement on onset laterality and spread presence with Gwet k, channels with Cohen k, and timing with the median absolute deviation (MAD). Interrater and majority vote consensus agreement were estimated with patient-clustered CIs. Results. Onset laterality showed substantial interrater agreement (Gwet k = 0.73, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.83); most disagreement involved bilateral onsets. Contralateral spread agreement was comparable (0.63, 0.48 to 0.76). Channel level agreement was higher for onset (inter rater Cohen k = 0.57) than for spread (0.38). Onset timing was highly consistent (median MAD 0.40 s); spread timing agreement was also high (1.99 s), but less so than onset timing (sign rank p < 0.001). Agreement did not differ across annotators or between temporal and non-temporal epilepsy. Significance. Epileptologists generally agree on onset laterality and whether and when seizures spread contralaterally, although spread channels are identified less reliably. These findings support the feasibility of measuring scalp EEG spread as a candidate noninvasive marker of seizure network extent. The public annotated dataset provides a multi-expert reference standard for developing automated spread detection algorithms.

papers.title: Individualized Atypicality of Structure-Function Configuration Marks Subthreshold Depression in Adolescents
papers.abstract: Background: Subthreshold depression (StD) in adolescence represents a critical state preceding major depressive disorder, yet its neurobiological substrates remain poorly characterized. Conventional structure-function coupling rely on DTI tractography, which produces non-isomorphic matrices and unstable single-subject estimates, limiting their clinical utility. We developed a novel isomorphic and multi-omics framework to quantify individualized structure-function configurations and tested whether adolescents with StD show reproducible deviations from a group-mean reference in a validation sample. Methods: We integrated five structural (cortical thickness, mean curvature, sulcal depth, fractional anisotropy, mean diffusivity) and five functional (ReHo, ALFF, CBF, local and global connectivity strength) features to construct regional SIND-FIND configurations using symmetric KL divergence in a discovery-validation design (N = 131). Individual typicality scores were defined as the correspondence between each participant's regional configuration profile and HC reference (Leave one out). The score has undergone parallel validations using conventional SC-FC coupling, molecular alignment (PET/AHBA), and behavioral correlations. Results: Group-mean configuration maps were spatially correlated across samples ({rho} = .93, pspin < .001). StD participants showed lower typicality than HC (F(1,94) = 8.73, p = .004); the conventional SC-FC comparison was not significant (F(1,92) = 3.31, p = .072). Regional differences involved frontoparietal and salience regions and aligned with PET (r = .55, pspin < .001) and AHBA (r = .47, pspin = .003) maps. After covariate adjustment, typicality correlated with SCL-90 ({rho} = -.262, q = .013), SDS ({rho} = -.234, q = .022), ISI ({rho} = -.296, q = .012) and PSQI ({rho} = -.288, q = .012; BH-FDR across five scales); coupling tracked depressive but not sleep symptoms (ISI {rho} = -.161, q = .124). Within validation StD participants, SCL-90 remained negatively associated with typicality ({rho} = -.42, p = .023). Conclusion: Our isomorphic, multimodal framework captures coordinated structures-function deviation in adolescent StD with greater group-effect sensitivity than conventional SC-FC coupling, together with regional specificity, molecular spatial alignment, and behavioral relevance. Configuration typicality, defined relative to an HC group-mean reference, may serve as an individual-level marker of organizational deviation during adolescence, pending larger, demographic stratified samples.

papers.title: Ultra-Processed Food Consumption and Physical, Cognitive and Academic Outcomes in Australian Early Adolescents Aged 10-14 Years: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Introduction. Ultra-processed foods (UPFs, NOVA Group 4) provide about half of the daily energy intake of Australian adolescents. Their links with adiposity are well studied. Far less is known about how UPF intake relates to cognition and school achievement in early adolescence, and no Australian study has examined physical, cognitive and academic outcomes together using the NOVA classification. Methods and analysis. This cross-sectional study will recruit approximately 650 students aged 10-14 years from schools sampled across Australian states and territories, stratified by jurisdiction, remoteness and socioeconomic status. Dietary intake will be assessed with two non-consecutive 24-hour recalls (ASA24-Australia), and UPF intake will be expressed as a percentage of total energy. Outcomes are measured BMI z-score, the CogState Brief Battery (Detection, Identification, One Card Learning, One Back) and NAPLAN Reading and Mathematics scores. Multilevel linear regression will account for clustering by school and adjust for socioeconomic position, maternal education, sleep, screen time, physical activity, age and sex. Mediation analysis will explore whether BMI z-score mediates UPF-cognition associations and whether cognition mediates UPF-NAPLAN associations. Ethics and dissemination. Approval will be sought from a university Human Research Ethics Committee and from state, territory, Catholic and independent school authorities before recruitment. Findings will be reported in peer-reviewed journals and at conferences, and summarised for schools, families and policymakers.

papers.title: Transportability of polysomnography-derived sleep physiological fingerprints across cohorts, measurement modalities and time: a four-axis evaluation in four cohorts
papers.abstract: Epidemiological evidence linking sleep to Alzheimer disease (AD) relies predominantly on self-reported sleep, whereas cohorts with polysomnography (PSG) and cohorts with AD biomarkers rarely share participants. Multifractal long-range-interdependency representations classify obstructive sleep apnoea severity accurately across cohorts, but whether such a physiological fingerprint can be transported between cohorts, between measurement modalities or over time has not been evaluated. We propose four axes of transportability and test them in the Sleep Heart Health Study (n = 5,614), MESA Sleep (n = 2,012), ADNI (n = 2,286) and MrOS Sleep (2,911 men; 1,026 re-examined after 6.37 years; 3,928 scored nights). Axis A1, cross-cohort construct convergence, passed: PSG-derived Sleep Coupling Disruption Index loadings agreed between SHHS and MESA (cosine 0.986; Wasserstein distance 0.0487). Axis A2, incremental validity beyond the apnoea-hypopnoea index, failed: the fully adjusted hazard ratio for incident cardiovascular disease was 1.009 (95% CI 0.941-1.085; p = 0.83) and the C-index was 0.8079 with or without the index; in MrOS, adding a multifractal coupling fingerprint increased R-squared by 0.00058 (likelihood-ratio p = 0.399). Axis A3, proxy identifiability, failed: the reliability ratio linking portable subjective complaints to objective physiological burden was 1.95 x 10-5, with a bootstrap 95% upper bound of 0.00261 and 0.0027 for a semantically optimised proxy, far below the 0.25 floor required for measurement-error correction. Under classical error this implies a 370-fold sample-size inflation; Monte-Carlo power at n = 10,000 was 0.177. A nominally significant association between night-time behaviour and dementia severity would require an implausible true physiological effect of 28.7 standard deviations, and it reversed to -0.0554 after adjustment for total neuropsychiatric burden. The prespecified ADNI primary outcome, plasma pTau217, was null (beta = 0.0033, p = 0.911), as were the MrOS six-year cognitive complaint outcome (beta = -0.0204, p = 0.375) and a 35-event self-reported dementia endpoint (OR = 0.921, p = 0.679). Axis A4, temporal stability, failed: six-year test-retest reliability was r = 0.157 (95% CI 0.096-0.216) for the fingerprint versus r = 0.455 (0.405-0.502) for AHI, despite stable concurrent validity (rho = 0.380 and 0.328 with same-night AHI). Spearman-Brown projection indicates that approximately nine nights must be averaged for the fingerprint to reach a reliability of 0.60, compared with two for AHI. A fingerprint can therefore be reproducible without being transportable. We provide a four-question decision workflow and an eight-item minimum reporting set; subjective sleep complaints should not be substituted for objective sleep physiology in aetiological inference.

papers.title: Sequential rTMS-tACS Neuromodulation Is Associated with Increased Resting-State Theta Activity in Fibromyalgia: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundSequential application of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) may induce neurophysiological changes within sensorimotor and pain-related networks. However, the resting-state EEG effects of this combined approach in fibromyalgia remain unknown. MethodsIn this exploratory randomized controlled pilot study, 10 adults with fibromyalgia were assigned to active stimulation (n = 5) or a no-stimulation control group (n = 5). Active participants received one or two sessions of 10-Hz rTMS over the left primary motor cortex (1,000 pulses/session), followed by 10 daily sessions of bilateral 10-Hz tACS (1 mA, 20 min). Six-minute eyes-closed resting-state EEG recordings were obtained before and after the intervention or an equivalent control interval. Power spectral density was quantified in the delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands and analyzed using mixed repeated-measures ANOVAs across central-centroparietal and posterior regions of interest. ResultsTheta power increased significantly in the active group but not in controls, yielding significant Time x Group (F(1,8)=8.70, p=.018, p{superscript 2}=.521) and Time x ROI x Group (F(1,8)=5.53, p=.047, p{superscript 2}=.409) interactions. Follow-up analyses showed increased theta power in both central-centroparietal (p=.004) and posterior (p=.012) regions, with a larger increase observed posteriorly. No significant interaction effects were found for delta, alpha, or beta power. ConclusionsSequential motor-cortex rTMS followed by repeated bilateral 10-Hz tACS was associated with increased resting-state theta activity in fibromyalgia. Given the small sample size, post hoc ROI selection, lack of sham stimulation, and absence of component-specific control conditions, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require replication in adequately powered sham-controlled studies.

papers.title: Generalizable mapping of the Epileptogenic Zone from interictal Intracranial EEG using an implant topology-aware Transformer
papers.abstract: Presurgical localization of the epileptogenic zone remains a central challenge in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. At the same time, the abundant interictal intracranial EEG (iEEG) data routinely acquired during presurgical evaluation remain an underexploited source of localizing information. We developed an iEEG implant topology-aware transformer that combines interictal iEEG features with electrode coordinates to predict resection targets. The model was trained exclusively on three public datasets (n = 476) and tested on cohorts from five independent centers across three countries (n = 216). In patients with favorable surgical outcomes (Engel I; n = 120), the median area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.71, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.92, outperforming interictal spike rate and clinically defined seizure-onset zone baselines in patients with favorable outcomes (P < 0.05 for both AUPRC and AUROC). Patients with unfavorable outcomes (Engel II-IV; n = 96) had lower prediction-resection alignment (median AUPRC, 0.42), and their highest confidence predictions were located farther from resected tissue (P = 0.005). These findings establish a generalizable framework that integrates neural activity and brain topology to identify epileptogenic tissue from interictal recordings, potentially improving surgical success rates and reducing reliance on resource-intensive seizure capture.

papers.title: Auricular Acupuncture for Erythematotelangiectatic Rosacea: Protocol for a Multicenter, Randomized, Participant- and Assessor-Masked, Sham-Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: Background: Persistent facial erythema and episodic flushing are prominent features of erythematotelangiectatic rosacea (ETR). The efficacy of auricular acupuncture (AA) for ETR is uncertain. Methods: This multicenter, randomized, participant- and assessor-masked, sham-controlled superiority trial was designed to enroll 108 adults aged 18 to 50 years with ETR and a baseline Clinician Erythema Assessment (CEA) score of at least 2 at 5 hospitals in China. Participants were allocated 1:1 to AA with semipermanent intradermal needles or visually matched, same-site nonpenetrating sham stimulation. Four auricular points (Shenmen, Sanjiao, Endocrine, and Heart) were treated on alternating ears every 3 days for 6 weeks, with self-pressure 3 times daily. Follow-up was scheduled through week 10. The primary outcome was clinician-rated erythema (CEA score) at week 6. Secondary outcomes comprised other clinician-rated erythema assessments, patient-rated redness, flushing, migraine symptoms, sleep quality, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and adverse events. The primary treatment contrast was planned using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance with multiple imputation for missing week 6 outcomes. Secondary longitudinal outcomes were planned for exploratory mixed-model analyses. Discussion: The trial was designed to assess the incremental efficacy and tolerability of penetrating auricular needling compared with a matched nonpenetrating procedure. Same-site pressure in both groups may have physiological effects, which should be considered when interpreting the results.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Automates Artifact Correction for Clinical Body Surface Gastric Mapping at Scale
papers.abstract: Body surface gastric mapping (BSGM) enables non-invasive measurement of gastric electrophysiology, but signals are approximately 100 times weaker than cardiac potentials and overlap spectrally with motion artifacts, necessitating labor-intensive manual review that limits clinical scalability. We present an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework to automate artifact correction in high-resolution BSGM. A signal reconstruction network was paired with a parallel uncertainty estimation network, trained on 2,398 multihour, 64-channel recordings from 27 international clinical sites using weak supervision, a physiology-aware loss function, and uncertainty-gated quality control. In an independent cohort of 127 patients, per-patient signal reconstruction error was 29% lower than with the industry-standard Wiener filter (10.3% vs 14.6%; lower in 103 patients), and remained lower when both filters retained identical samples (9.8% vs 14.6%). Amplitude-movement correlation was 23% lower. Changing only the filter raised the rhythm index across the cohort and robustly altered automated clinical phenotyping in 7.1% of patients, mostly by removing dysrhythmic classifications from artifact-affected recordings. Uncertainty-aware deep learning enables reliable automated artifact correction in body surface gastric mapping, improving signal fidelity and enabling scalable clinical interpretation. The system is FDA-cleared (510(k) K252504) and deployed in clinical practice, demonstrating that data-driven artifact correction can meet regulatory requirements for medical devices and reduce dependence on specialist manual review.
